label: TSMM to ODRL experimental binding
description: Maps ODRL policy-expression concepts into TSMM abstractions so policy artifacts can be compared and carried across trust-system implementations without treating ODRL as the complete trust-governance model.

mappings.description: Machine-readable policy object that groups rules governing what may, must, or must not happen for a target asset or service.
Allowed action statement interpreted as a policy rule that can support a downstream trust decision when combined with identity, authority, and evidence.
Disallowed action statement interpreted as a policy rule limiting acceptable behavior or permitted effects.
Required action or pre-condition attached to permission or obligation semantics.
Actors referenced by policy rules. In TSMM these remain role-bearing trust participants whose authority still needs contextual interpretation.
Policy target or governed resource. Depending on context, TSMM may model the governed object as an artifact, service, credential, or other trust-bearing asset.
conditions: ODRL target does not force a single TSMM class. The correct TSMM interpretation depends on what is being governed.

mappings.description: Boolean or logical expression that refines when a rule applies.
Community-specific extension and interpretation surface that constrains policy semantics for a bounded ecosystem.

notes: ODRL is valuable in TSMM as a policy-expression surface, not as a replacement for governance, assurance, delegation, or lifecycle semantics.
This binding is intentionally experimental because policy publication and policy enforcement remain separate concerns.
The binding helps TSMM compare policy-bearing ecosystems while preserving the distinction between machine-readable rules and trustworthy execution.

guarantees.name: policy-object-modeling
guarantees.description: ODRL Policy, Rule, Action, Party, Asset, and Constraint concepts can be represented through TSMM policy-facing abstractions.

guarantees.name: profile-aware-comparison
guarantees.description: ODRL profiles can be compared as bounded ecosystem interpretations instead of ad hoc local policy vocabularies.

guarantees.name: runtime-governance-completeness
guarantees.description: ODRL contributes policy expression, but not the full runtime authority, evidence, assessment, revocation, and trust-effect semantics carried by TSMM.

limitations.name: publication-enforcement-gap
limitations.impact: Publishing an ODRL policy does not prove that the policy is evaluated or enforced during operation.
limitations.mitigation: Pair ODRL policy artifacts with evidence, verifier outputs, logs, and domain-specific control systems where execution trust matters.

limitations.name: delegation-scope-gap
limitations.impact: ODRL can describe permissions and duties but does not by itself model bounded delegated authority chains for agentic systems.
limitations.mitigation: Use TSMM delegation, authority-graph, and lifecycle surfaces alongside ODRL policy objects.

limitations.name: asset-model-overreach
limitations.impact: Not every trust-relevant object in TSMM naturally reduces to ODRL asset usage semantics.
limitations.mitigation: Treat ODRL as a bounded policy carrier for selected artifact and service surfaces rather than the universal abstraction for the entire stack.

behavioralExpectations.expectation: Implementers treat ODRL as the machine-readable policy layer and avoid inferring broader governance legitimacy, assurance strength, or delegated authority solely from ODRL publication.
Downstream schema and baseline repos preserve policy references, target identifiers, party roles, and profile references so ODRL artifacts remain portable without semantic drift.

notes: Suitable for comparative modelling and for bounded policy-carrier use.
Not a replacement for TSMM delegation, evidence, assessment, or lifecycle semantics.
Policy publication MUST NOT be treated as equivalent to policy enforcement.
